slides.say: Welcome to Data Science from Scratch. Lesson one: what is data science, really?

slides.text: Turning raw data into insights and better decisions.
slides.say: Data science is the practice of turning raw data into useful insights, and better decisions.

slides.sub: Reason about data · work with it at scale · know which questions matter
slides.say: It sits where three things meet. Statistics, to reason about data. Programming, to work with it at scale. And domain knowledge, to know which questions actually matter.

slides.text: Question → Collect → Clean → Explore → Model → Communicate
slides.say: Most projects follow the same loop. Ask a question. Collect the data. Clean it. Explore it. Build a model if you need one. Then communicate what you found.

slides.text: Cleaning data is often the most time-consuming part.
slides.say: And here's what surprises most beginners: cleaning and preparing the data is often the most time-consuming part of the job.

slides.sub: Past repayment records → clean → find patterns → model → better lending decisions
slides.say: For example, a lender might ask: which customers are likely to repay? A data scientist gathers past repayment records, cleans them, finds patterns, and builds a model to support that decision.

slides.text:
Data science isn't just models.
It's asking good questions of data.
slides.say: So remember: data science isn't just about models. It's about asking good questions of data.

slides.text: Types of data, and why they matter.
slides.say: Next lesson: the different types of data, and why they matter.

summary: Data science turns raw data into insights and better decisions by combining statistics, programming and domain knowledge.
practice: Pick a decision you make often (for example, what to buy, or when to leave for work). Write down one question data could help you answer, and list the data you would need to collect.
